title: rag-lab ops page: choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned The Wire Desk. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Wire Desk
options.lineage: 1960s-80s newsroom wire desk: teletype copy, canary copy paper, the editor's blue pencil and the spike
options.thesis: Every question is a story assignment; three wires file their ranked copy and the desk shows exactly what runs and why.
materials: canary teletype copy paper with sprocket margins
the HOLD FOR LEGAL rubber stamp
options.viewport: Assignment line across the top (your question), three wire columns below it (DENSE, BM25, HYBRID) each a strip of teletype copy ranked 1 to k with real scores, the editor's blue-pencil lines joining the same chunk across wires; the planted chunk arrives stamped HOLD FOR LEGAL.
options.risk: Can read as nostalgic costume if the paper texture outweighs the data; the rankings must stay the loudest thing.

raised.raise: One type size for all copy: rank is carried by weight, case, reversal and rule, never by font size.
Each corpus source gets one fixed colour code on its slug, so the same README is recognisable across all three wires at a glance.
One control re-files every wire at once: change the question or k and all three columns re-rank together, live.

options.label: Gel Lanes
options.thesis: Each retriever is a lane; every chunk is a band that lands at its rank, so the same chunk lines up (or doesn't) across lanes.
options.viewport: A dark gel slab with three lanes plus a ladder lane of corpus sources; bands glow at their rank; the injected chunk shows as a red contaminant band.
options.risk: The most familiar 'science lab' metaphor, and dark plus one glowing accent sits near a common AI look.

options.label: Lexicon Page
options.lineage: nineteenth-century lexicon with shoulder index and colour plates
options.thesis: Retrieved chunks as lexicon entries, ranked by how much apparatus each is granted; sources as the thumb index.
options.viewport: Guide words name the question; three columns of entries; the shoulder index marks which READMEs were reached.
options.case: Fuses cleanly because the corpus is prose; loses on audience identification for a DevOps learner.
options.risk: Cream plus serif is a default look; needs strict plates to avoid it.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.lineage: 1971 pocket airline timetable on a light table
options.viewport: A lateral rack of slides, one per retriever.
options.risk: Airline world collides with order-lab's departures board.
options.case: Loses both axes: airline imagery belongs to order-lab, and the rake hurts reading ranks.
options.kept: One type size, rank by weight, case and reversal.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Every chunk a catalog number, sources colour-coded.
options.risk: Codes hide meaning from a learner.
options.case: Loses both: decoding hurts a learning tool.
options.kept: A fixed colour code per source.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.thesis: One slider remaps the whole grid live.
options.viewport: A giant glyph and a breathing grid.
options.case: Loses both: nothing in RAG is a glyph.
options.kept: One control re-ranks everything at once.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A RAG playground: chat box, sources panel, a metrics table.
canonCard.viewport: Question box on top, answer card, collapsible sources, eval table in a tab.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every RAG demo by design.
